I submitted an equal-weight portfolio of all 423 signals. I don't expect it to beat zero: its training Sharpe is −0.16 and it got a FAIL on validation, the only validation check I ran.

**Why I didn't search for a PASS:** The training data shows no real edge anywhere. Across the 423 signals, Sharpe ratios spread with a standard deviation of 0.19, which is about what pure noise over 30 years would give (0.18). The best one, `ma_Steel_5_21` at 0.57, is about the size you'd expect from the luckiest of 423 noise series. Rankings also don't carry over: the 20 best signals in 1970–84 averaged a Sharpe of −0.18 in 1985–99, and signal Sharpes from separate time periods are slightly negatively correlated. With up to 200 tries and the run stopping at the first PASS, I'd most likely just find a lucky portfolio that wouldn't hold up after 2013. So I chose a portfolio that involves no selection and checked validation once.

The equal-weight portfolio of all 423 signals (each one an industry hedged against the market) has a training Sharpe of −0.16 and failed validation. I chose it on purpose: training data shows no persistent edge in any signal, so a diversified portfolio picked with no selection is the most honest choice, and its expected Sharpe from 2013 on is about zero.
